ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart robot that can do lots of things, like play games or answer questions. But, you know what? Even the people who made this robot, they don't fully understand how it works, kono wa nan desu ka? (what is this?)

It's like building a really complex Lego castle, but you don't know how all the pieces fit together, ne? (right?) The creators of these neural networks and AIs, they're like the Lego builders, but they don't know the secret formula, you know? (you know?)

These networks are made up of many layers of interconnected nodes, or "neurons," that process information in a way that's not fully understood, desu ka? (isn't it?) Even the people who created them, they're not entirely sure how the nodes talk to each other, or how the information flows through the network, you see? (you see?)

It's like trying to explain a dream to someone, but you don't fully understand it yourself, kono yūgen wa nan desu ka? (what is this mysterious feeling?) The creators of these AIs are like, "Hey, this thing works, but I don't know why," and that's okay, desu ka? (isn't it?)

So, even though the creators of these neural networks and AIs are really smart, they don't fully understand how they work, and that's okay, you know? (you know?) It's like trying to solve a really hard puzzle, but you don't know the answer, ne? (right?)
